summary.headline: True Colors H1 FY27 revenue rose 21.1% to INR 183.01 crore, with PAT up 43.3% to INR 21.09 crore as consumables drove margins.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 21.1% YoY to INR 183.01 crore, and profit grew roughly twice as fast, with EBITDA up 40.1% to INR 32.34 crore and EBITDA margin up 240 bps to 17.7%. Management attributed the margin gain to a richer mix of ink and paper, which made up 56.2% of revenue versus 48.7% a year earlier. Operating cash flow turned positive at INR 27.16 crore against an outflow of INR 10.90 crore last year. Management announced a 50:50 JV with Swastik Strategic Ventures LLP for a pulp-to-coated-paper plant at Bardoli (INR 320-340 crore) and began in-house ink production plans under INKIA.

financial_highlights.change: vs outflow of INR 10.90 crore in H1 FY26
broadly stable; INR 111 crore cited at FY26 end

segments.name: Sublimation paper
segments.commentary: Volume more than doubled to 9.97 crore meters (from 4.92 crore); revenue +79% to INR 51.81 crore, now 28% of total revenue. Coating capacity 2 crore meters/month, fully utilised.

segments.name: INKIA ink
segments.commentary: Volume +22% to 689 tons; currently supplying more than 150 tons/month versus about 58 tons/month in FY24. Management also cited 80 tons/month of INKIA production, with ITACA (Spain) premium pigment ink commercial supplies starting this half.

segments.name: Digital printing fabrics
segments.commentary: Volume +7% to 99.71 lakh meters; revenue +25% to INR 49.12 crore on better product mix.

segments.name: Machines
segments.commentary: 56 units installed vs 68 a year ago; active installed base +11% to 956 machines. Management said machine sales are lumpy and the lowest-margin line (around 5% of gross margin).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-22% reaffirmed.
Management expects H2 FY27 profitability to track H1 gains; said machine-heavy periods can pull margin down.

INKIA Phase-1 in-house ink capacity of 150 tons/month targeted by end FY27 at capex of about INR 40-45 crore, eligible for 35% subsidy under Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026; Phase-2 to 500 tons/month in FY28 and 1,000 tons/month longer term.

Paper JV (True Colors Advanced Materials Pvt Ltd) at Bardoli: 8-10 crore meters/month, ~29 GSM coated media, commercial production targeted H2 FY29; project cost INR 320-340 crore, funded 25% equity / 75% project debt at JV level, True Colors share of equity 50% of 25%.
capex_capacity: Coating capacity at 2 crore meters/month, already at optimum utilisation; was 30 lakh meters/month three years ago.
INKIA Phase-1: 150 tons/month by end FY27, capex INR 40-45 crore; Phase-2: 500 tons/month in FY28.
Paper JV at Bardoli, Gujarat: pulp-to-coated-media integrated plant, 8-10 crore meters/month, project cost INR 320-340 crore; commercial production targeted H2 FY29.
Management cited a 25% capital subsidy for the paper project and 35% for the ink plant under Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026.
INKIA Inks Pvt Ltd (about 80 tons/month) to be merged into True Colors under NCLT process; merger consolidated from April 2026 per management.
demand_pricing: Management said ink realisations are falling globally as volumes rise, which explains revenue lagging volume growth in ink.
Management estimates True Colors holds 16-18% of India's digital fabric printing volume; digital is 8-9% of Indian textile printing vs 80-95% in Europe.
India imports about 70-75% of its sublimation paper, mainly from China; management cited about 29 GSM Chinese coated paper as the benchmark.
Installed base mix is 70-75% sublimation and 25-30% reactive; management expects a move toward 60:40 within 4-5 years.
Management said receivable cycle is 90-120 days, which it called normal for the industry, versus 60-90 days earlier; receivables over 180 days not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to raise equity, and how will the paper JV be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said projects have been funded through internal accrual and project debt, with equity not ruled out at company level. JV equity is 50% of 25% of INR 320-340 crore (about INR 40 crore for True Colors), which management said can come from internal accrual or bank debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising faster than revenue, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the receivable base is INR 116 crore vs INR 111 crore a year ago on higher revenue, and that the 90-120 day cycle is normal. Bill discounting and channel financing are being explored, with no quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: What margin does each business line earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated EBITDA is about 17%, in a 14-18% band; consumables, ink, paper and printing run at similar margins, with machines the lowest margin (about 5% of gross margin). Segment-level margins were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why move into base paper manufacturing, which is a commodity business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV targets ultra-low 29 GSM specialty sublimation media, not commodity base paper, because Indian mills cannot produce below 32 GSM. It said the output is for the company's ecosystem and not for paper mills.

qa_highlights.question: How much of INKIA's output goes to True Colors, and can INKIA's financials be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35-40% of INKIA's output went to the True Colors ecosystem last year, with the rest sold to other distributors; ecosystem consumption averages 115 tons/month. INKIA standalone H1 numbers were not shared pending regulatory confirmation.

qa_highlights.question: What valuation was used for the INKIA merger share swap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the valuation used FY26 PAT of about INR 4 crore on revenue of INR 24 crore, at a 15x multiple, for INR 60 crore at INR 240 per share, with the transfer to be priced at the share price at NCLT approval.

risks_watch: Receivables of INR 116 crore on 90-120 day cycles; management has not given a receivable ageing figure above 180 days.
Ink realisation pressure from global price corrections may keep revenue growth below volume growth.
Execution risk on the INR 320-340 crore paper JV, which is a new business for True Colors with a partner (Swastik) that was formed only in October 2026.
Related-party items: INKIA was promoter-owned at formation and is being merged at a 15x PE valuation, while the stock trades at about 8x PE per an analyst.
Management said H2 margin could fall if machine sales rise, because consumable mix drives margins; INKIA merger financials not yet disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the H1 numbers and the consumables thesis, but guarded on specifics: management declined to give segment margins, INKIA financials, or the paper JV's EBITDA per meter, and deferred several questions to later updates.
key_quotes: When profits grow at twice the rate of revenue, it tells you something about the quality of that revenue.
Our business model is more like selling a razor and then make money from the blades, or either supplying a printer just like HP do.
So we are not competing with any of the Indian paper mills or globally any of the paper mills.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-22% was reaffirmed (midpoint 21%), backed by H1 revenue up 21.1% and the sublimation coating line already fully utilised; INKIA Phase-1 (150 t/month, INR 40-45 cr) is targeted by end FY27 and the Bardoli paper JV (INR 320-340 cr) by H2 FY29, but no quarterly figures for Q2 alone were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management aims to sustain the H1 EBITDA margin of about 17% (up 240 bps to 17.7%) in H2 on the richer ink and paper mix (56.2% of revenue vs 48.7%), but this depends on machine mix and the 14-18% band.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: end FY27 (INKIA Ph-1); H2 FY29 (paper JV)
rows.why: INKIA Phase-1 of 150 t/month at INR 40-45 cr is targeted by end FY27, and the Bardoli paper JV (INR 320-340 cr, 8-10 cr meters/month) is targeted for H2 FY29; coating line at 2 cr meters/month is already fully utilised.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 sublimation paper volume more than doubled to 9.97 cr meters, ink volume rose 22% to 689 t, and digital fabric volume rose 7%; FY27 revenue growth of 20-22% was reaffirmed, though the coating line is at optimum utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The 50:50 JV with Swastik for the INR 320-340 cr Bardoli paper plant and INKIA Phase-1 capex (INR 40-45 cr) are already announced, with Phase-2 (500 t/month) slated for FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-22% was only reaffirmed (H1 at +21.1%), with no raise signalled, and management said it will stick to that guideline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said H2 margin could fall if machine sales rise (machines are about 5% of gross margin), and ink realisations are falling globally, so revenue can lag volume.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ITACA (Spain) premium pigment ink commercial supplies start this half, and the Bardoli JV targets 29 GSM specialty sublimation media for the ecosystem by H2 FY29.

rows.label: INKIA Phase-1 subsidy and in-house ink
rows.why: INKIA Phase-1 capex of INR 40-45 cr is eligible for a 35% subsidy under Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026, and in-house production of 80 t/month is already running, versus 150 t/month targeted by end FY27.

rows.label: Receivables and bill discounting
rows.why: Receivables are INR 116 cr on a 90-120 day cycle (vs 60-90 days earlier), and bill discounting and channel financing are being explored with no quantified target; ageing above 180 days was not disclosed.

rows.label: INKIA merger into True Colors
rows.why: INKIA Inks (about 80 t/month) is being merged at INR 60 cr (15x FY26 PAT of about INR 4 cr), with consolidation from April 2026 per management, but standalone financials have not been shared.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 growth, margins and the consumables thesis and reaffirmed the 20-22% FY27 guide, but was guarded on segment margins, INKIA financials and the paper JV's economics.
